newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Groups seek Saudi mercy for Pakistan children.
newsitem.headline: Groups seek Saudi mercy for Pakistan children.

text.p: Amnesty International and two Pakistani women's groups urged Saudi Arabia on Thursday to show leniency to several Pakistani children and women arrested for drug offences.

A statement received in Islamabad from the London-based human rights group asked the Saudi government to immediately clarify the fate of seven Pakistani children arrested with eight women and four men -- all of whom may face the death penalty.
It also urged the Pakistani government "not to shirk its responsibility towards these children who are currently being held in Saudi Arabian jails and to ensure that they are not sentenced to death".
In Islamabad, members of the local Progressive Women's Association (PWA) and Auran (woman) Foundation demonstrated outside the Saudi embassy calling for leniency for the arrested children and women.
Saudi Arabia enforces Islamic sharia law by publicly beheading convicted murderers, drug smugglers and rapists.

Amnesty said it was not known whether the 19 Pakistanis, arrested on January 19 at Jeddah airport for allegedly concealing heroin, had been tried, convicted and sentenced to death, or if they had been permitted legal counsel during trial.

"The places and conditions of their detention also remain unclear," Amnesty said. "The government of Saudi Arabia has so far failed to respond to Amnesty International's appeals to clarify their legal status."
Pakistani Interior Minister Shujaat Hussain said last week he had twice sent requests for clemency for the arrested children and women to his Saudi counterpart, Prince Nayef bin Abdul Aziz.
